notes: New derived edit (2026-11-12), replacing the Aage Bohr edit: every model missed the Christian Bohr premise. Prince William's paternal grandfather is the stock example of a fact worked out from two stored ones (Charles is William's father, Philip is Charles's father). Rating: the exact phrase is almost absent from the corpus (1, 2 and 30 hits) though Wikipedia uses it once in an anecdote, so the claim is derived with that caveat. Related near and far ask what the edit overturns on the old value's side (William a grandson of Philip; George a great-grandson of Philip), both stored; a model could still answer the maternal side differently, so the near question lists the revision fact that Philip was not William's maternal grandfather. The premise-route question reaches William as Prince George's father (binding): a model that keeps both premises answers Prince Philip there. The indeterminate question asks Charles III's father (w1 Philip, w2 George VI); w1 is also the answer of a model that did not edit.
